title: Sparse Reward Subsystem in Large Language Models
claim: A small set of identifiable units in a model mirrors a biological subsystem, with distinct signals that support distinct downstream applications.
layout: 3 columns-ish: left analogy panel, right two color-coded rows of signal plus application
description: A wide figure with a gray left sidebar and two tinted bands on the right. The sidebar shows a brain cartoon with a blue OFC dot and an orange VTA/SNc dot. Below it, definitions of value and dopamine neurons are linked by an 'Analogy' arrow to a grid of LLM hidden-state dots with a few blue and orange ones highlighted. The blue band covers value neurons. It has a line plot of value for correct versus wrong answers, and a confidence-prediction mini-pipeline from a question document through value neurons to a gauge. The orange band covers dopamine neurons. It has activation traces with green peak highlights and a red trough highlight, and a tree of candidate steps being scored and pruned into a guided search. Blue and orange color coding ties the whole figure together.
caption: Overview of the sparse reward subsystem in LLMs. The left panel illustrates a computational analogy with biological value and dopamine neurons. Value neurons encode the value of the current state, while dopamine neurons encode step-level TD errors. The signal illustrations show value estimates tracking the chance of success (\S[ref]) and dopamine-neuron activations exhibiting peaks and troughs at unexpected progress and reasoning errors (\S[ref]). We apply value neurons to confidence prediction (\S[ref]) and dopamine neurons to process-reward-guided search (\S[ref]).
abstract: Recent studies show that LLM hidden states encode reward-related information, such as answer correctness and model confidence. However, existing approaches typically fit black-box probes on the full hidden states, offering little insight into how this information is structured across neurons. In this paper, we show that reward-related information is concentrated in a sparse subset of neurons. Using simple probing, we identify two types of neurons: value neurons, whose activations predict state value, and dopamine neurons, whose activations encode step-level temporal difference (TD) errors. Together, these neurons form a sparse reward subsystem within LLM hidden states. These names are drawn by analogy with neuroscience, where value neurons and dopamine neurons in the biological reward subsystem also encode value and reward prediction errors, respectively. We demonstrate that value neurons are robust and transferable across diverse datasets and models, and provide causal evidence that they encode reward-related information. Finally, we show applications of the reward subsystem: value neurons serve as effective predictors of model confidence, and dopamine neurons can function as a process reward model (PRM) to guide inference-time search. Our code is available at https://github.com/zou-group/reward_subsystem.
